messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: Fitting hierarchical models with the R package brms
parts:
Dear list members,

I was wondering whether it would be possible to fit occupancy models (or other hierarchical models) with the R package brms.

The brms package fit Bayesian generalized (non-)linear multivariate multilevel models using 'Stan' for full Bayesian inference, and is very flexible very well supported in the R community.

Does anybody in the list have an insight on this?

Thank you very much in advance.

Manuel

messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: Re: Fitting hierarchical models with the R package brms
parts:
I futzed around with this for a bit while sitting in on a day of Darryl MacKenzie’s excellent workshop.  I was unfortunately unable to attend the whole thing, as I had a few other obligations, but you can see a small bit of something I whipped up comparing RPrseence and results from brms. In the code, stan files are also generated as output. I admit, I stopped after the simplest example (as I was no longer at the workshop), but I think you can see where it would go from there.

https://www.dropbox.com/s/0wl1q59iqczsfl2/weta_compare.html?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/71qz7aar2kd7jr5/weta_compare.Rmd?dl=0

I don’t claim deep expertise here (and feel free to point out where some of this is wrong), but I hope this might be a starting point for your efforts.

Yes, that answered my question.  I guess once you are in brms, you can use other functions from brms and other package for plotting and model diagnostics and evaluation. 

If you (list members) don't mind, I can direct the same question (crossposting) to the Stan forum, which include brms, to see the response from somebody in the forum, and may be Paul Bürkner, the developer of the package, can add some insight.

Manuel
